summary: Terms Acceptance Report (admin) + Driver Independent Courier Terms gate + Merchant terms gate tested end-to-end on the preview host. Backend: 12/12 pytest pass (auth 401/403, report shape, remind 200 -> 429 cooldown, 409 all-accepted, 404 unknown, driver & merchant terms-status/accept flows, admin accept 403, report reflects acceptance with matching timestamp). Frontend (375x667): admin-terms-link -> /admin/terms works, stores/drivers pills, ALL/PENDING/ACCEPTED filters filter correctly, EMAIL REMINDER shows green toast 'REMINDER SENT...' and 'Last reminder ...' line; second tap shows red 'A reminder was already sent today'. Driver Marcus: terms-modal blocks route (taps behind blocked), checkbox/accept disabled until scrolled to end, accept closes modal, reload doesn't re-show, Sign out returns to driver sign-in. Bakery sees store terms modal, accepts -> 'THANKS · TERMS ACCEPTED' toast, no modal on reload; Bay Books sees no modal. Admin report then shows Bakery + Marcus accepted with timestamps. Found one stacking bug: BadgeCelebration overlay renders ON TOP of the terms modal. No deprecated packages detected.

minor.issue: Terms acceptance is enforced only client-side (TermsGate). A driver who hasn't accepted DRIVER_TERMS_VERSION can still call manifest/stop endpoints directly (or with an old app build). Consider a server-side check on driver shift actions (e.g. route start / arrive / deliver) returning 403 'accept terms' like the PHIPA consent gate.
Merchant users list uses x['email'] (KeyError -> 500 if a merchant user ever lacks email). Use x.get('email'). Low risk.

ui_bugs.issue: For a driver with new weekly badges (Priya drv-2) the full-screen 'NEW WEEKLY BADGES UNLOCKED' celebration renders above the terms modal (elementFromPoint at terms-cancel = badge-celebration-dismiss). Driver must dismiss a celebration before seeing the blocking terms. Suppress BadgeCelebration (and other overlays) while terms-status.required is true.

issues: For a driver with no PHIPA consent AND no terms (tested drv-3 temporarily), consent-modal and terms-modal are mounted at the same time (terms on top, consent behind). Works sequentially, but two back-to-back legal modals, and ConsentModal also has its own consent-terms-checkbox -> terms agreed twice. Consider explicit sequencing or merging into one step.
Leftover TEST_Store (mer-a14d11dc, test_store_46ef85@example.com) from an earlier iteration appears as a pending store in the report (test-data pollution).

action_items: Hide/defer BadgeCelebration (and any other driver overlays) until the driver terms are accepted so the terms modal is topmost.
Sequence DriverConsentGate (PHIPA) and TermsGate so only one legal modal is mounted at a time (or merge), avoid double terms checkbox.
Optional: enforce driver terms acceptance server-side on shift actions; use x.get('email') in terms_report.
Optional: remove leftover TEST_Store merchant/user test data.
critical_code_review_comments: TermsGate react-query key ['terms-status', kind] is not cleared on sign-out; refetch-on-mount (staleTime 0) hides it - tested driver A accept -> sign out -> driver B sign in: modal showed with no flash.
terms_remind checks 20h cooldown (429) before the all-accepted check (409); fine but a store that accepted after a reminder returns 429 instead of 409 for 20h (cosmetic, button is hidden anyway).
test_terms_acceptance.py must run with -n 0 (pytest-xdist default here races the shared demo-user fixture).

success_rate.frontend: 95% (all requested flows pass; 1 overlay stacking bug)

rca_of_issue: Badge overlay over terms: BadgeCelebration is rendered inside driver/[driverId].tsx with its own Modal/absolute overlay that mounts after TermsGate's Modal (TermsGate is in driver/_layout.tsx), so on web it is later in the DOM portal order and paints on top.
